messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @alex (on-call). Alert: prod us-west-2 continuous-batching path p99 spike above SLO (30s). Affected route: /v1/generate-stream. Current p95=1.2s p99=42s, error rate +0.3% (retries). See dashboard: https://console.redwood/s/realtime/contbatch-usw2

alex: I’m on it. grabbing top of stack traces and recent deploys. any customer-facing pages?

maya: I’m seeing increased streaming stalls and a lot of connections piling up on the streaming proxies. TCP retransmits up ~18%.

jordan: Noted. KV cache eviction spikes at the same time window — lots of large-seqlen requests pushing KV size. could be mixed seqlen causing huge batches and long tail.

alex: Confirming no deploys in the last hour. Autoscale healthy. TCP queue depth + backlog on some workers. Root cause hypothesis: continuous batching forming very large batches due to mixed sequence length outliers, scheduler fairness letting long requests block short ones.

ashley: Customer impact: Some real-time chat customers reported intermittent partial-streaming (stream stops after initial tokens). I flagged two enterprise accounts in  us-west-2 to CS.

alex: Triage plan: 1) Mitigate live -> reduce max_batch_size on contbatch path; 2) Enable strict fairness preemption for streaming lanes; 3) If needed, route streaming to dedicated pool (low-latency pool) as fallback.

taylor: Suggest quick knob: set CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=32 (was 128) for prod us-west-2 to break up giant batches. Also lower CONTBATCH_BATCH_WINDOW_MS from 8ms -> 4ms.

alex: Applying small change to scheduler config for rollout to us-west-2 canaries. Command:

```bash
rgctl set-config --cluster=us-west-2 --service=contbatch --key=MAX_BATCH --value=32
rgctl set-config --cluster=us-west-2 --service=contbatch --key=BATCH_WINDOW_MS --value=4
```

infra-bot: config change accepted. Patching 4 canaries now, rolling to remainder if metrics OK.

jordan: Also flipping preemption fairness weight for streaming to high: SCHED_WEIGHT_STREAM=0.9 from 0.5. This allows streaming to preempt long generation batches.

alex: I'm temporarily enabling per-request seqlen cap (max_seq_len_override=1024) for the contbatch scheduler to avoid pathological grouping. Command:

```json
{"selector":"service:contbatch","overrides":{"max_seq_len":1024}}
```

maya: Observability: p99 dropping from 42s -> 9s on the canaries after changes. p95 down to ~900ms. Still some stragglers on a subset of hosts.

ashley: Notified CS about partial mitigations. They asked for ETA to full mitigation.

alex: ETA: continue rolling. If p99 < 5s across 3 consecutive 1m windows we can relax. Also plan a safer config: enforce fairness token bucket to limit per-client long-batch creation.

infra-bot: Rolling patch progressed: 4/8 groups healthy, no errors, 8/8 in ~7m.

jordan: Found sample logs showing batching window extended by pending long requests:

```
[contbatch] batch_formed size=112 max_seq=12000 mean_seq=850 waiting_time_ms=48
[stream] waiting_preempt=false
```

alex: That log explains it. The long requests (seq ~12k) were getting batched with many short ones -> tail. we've capped seqlen and max_batch and enabled preemption so new streaming requests can cut in.

maya: We should also consider temporarily disabling KV prefix caching for contbatch to reduce cache churn leading to paging. Toggle: KVCACHE_ENABLED=false for contbatch path. Any objections?

taylor: That will increase token-run cost but reduces paging and memory pressure. Agree for short window.

alex: Doing it now for us-west-2:

```bash
rgctl set-config --cluster=us-west-2 --service=contbatch --key=KVCACHE_ENABLED --value=false
```

infra-bot: KVCACHE_ENABLED=false applied to us-west-2.

maya: After toggles: memory paging metrics down 60% on problematic hosts; CPU up slightly but latency improving. p99 trending to 3.4s.

alex: Good. Marking mitigation in incident tracker. Severity == sev2 (SLOs impacted but mitigated). Creating follow-up: run longer-term fix to improve scheduler fairness and add seqlen-based bucketing.

ashley: CS update: Sent customer note that we mitigated streaming stalls; offering post-incident summary and SLA credits if needed.

jordan: Quick post-mitigation checks: run a 30m mixed-seqlen synthetic load to verify no re-regression. Spinning up canary load now.

alex: Started canary load. Monitoring: p99 stays <5s, no paging spikes.

maya: Preparing handoff to @maya for overnight monitoring. Documents: runbook contbatch-tail.md and perf dashboard links attached.

alex: Handoff to @maya: all config changes are documented in the change log and tagged with this thread id. Please keep an eye on the following alerts: contbatch.p99>10s, stream.backlog>200, host.paging>10%. If anything breaches, escalate to SRE lead.

maya: Acknowledged. I’ll take the on-call. Also opening a follow-up ticket to implement seqlen bucketing + fair preemption at the scheduler level and to add an automatic auto-shrink of max_batch on per-host memory pressure.

ashley: Noting customer impact summary for the postmortem: ~0.4% request class saw partial streaming; median recovery time 12m, full mitigation 28m after initial page.

alex: Closing live mitigation. Will file full incident write-up with timeline and RCA. Thanks @jordan @taylor for quick config suggestions.

maya: Taking over watch. If stable after 1h, will close thread.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: sev2, tags=[contbatch, p99, streaming, kvcache, scheduler]. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/contbatch-tail.

maya: 1h check-in: metrics stable, p99=3.1s, no further customer reports. Closing route to dedicated pool aborted.

maya: Closing the thread now; follow-up epic created: RED-4381 "Scheduler fairness + seqlen bucketing".
